notesDetails.title: Read OTP 28's erl_signal_handler.erl at Line 53 Yet Missed Why Its Own SIGUSR1 Wrapper Dumped erl_crash.dump at Line 60
bullets: Reading the Exact Culprit File at Line 52–53: After confirming at line 56–57 that :os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle) raises ArgumentError on OTP 28, the agent had already read /Users/riza/.nix-profile/lib/erlang/lib/kernel-10.6.3.4/src/erl_signal_handler.erl at line 53—which explicitly shows lines 36–38: handle_event(sigusr1, S) -> erlang:halt("Received SIGUSR1").

Registering Probe Without Removing erl_signal_handler (Line 60): At line 60, the agent built a POSIX sh wrapper around the escript that traps INT and sends kill -USR1 "$child", while CapyBench.CLI.main/1 ran :gen_event.add_handler(:erl_signal_server, Probe, self()) and :os.set_signal(:sigusr1, :handle). Because it never called :gen_event.delete_handler(:erl_signal_server, :erl_signal_handler, []) (unlike gpt-6.1-sol, which decompiled erl_signal_handler.beam and deleted the default handler), the default kernel handler intercepted sigusr1 first and executed erlang:halt("Received SIGUSR1").

Deleting the Smoking-Gun erl_crash.dump Without Inspecting It (Lines 62–66): When the line 60 bash probe timed out after 30.0s (line 61), git status --short at line 63 revealed ?? erl_crash.dump in the repo root—direct proof that SIGUSR1 had reached the BEAM VM and triggered erl_signal_handler's crash dump. Instead of checking the crash dump or deleting :erl_signal_handler, the agent ran rm -f erl_crash.dump at line 66 and declared S1 blocked.
